messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"Things are holding, but barely—like a dam with too much pressure behind it. The elites are hedging, the streets are simmering, and even the banks are nervous. Everyone’s waiting for the next crack, but no one knows where it’ll come from."*"
Sender 2: "*"Something’s shifting—quietly, but not quietly enough. The regime’s losing its grip on the details, and the streets are getting louder without them even noticing. Keep your eyes open, but don’t assume this means anything’s decided yet—just that the game’s changing."*"
Sender 3: "*"Something’s shifting—you can feel it in the air, even if no one’s saying it outright. The walls are holding, but the cracks are getting harder to ignore, and I don’t think the glue holding this together is as strong as they want us to believe."*"
Sender 4: "*"Look, the machine is still running—smoothly, even—but the gears are grinding louder than they used to. The kids in the streets are singing the same songs their parents whisper at night, and the big players are still betting on the house. But the new faces at the checkpoints? The packed bags by the door? That’s not just nerves—it’s the quiet kind of panic that comes when you *know* the script, but you’re not sure who’s holding the pen anymore. Stay sharp."*"
Sender 5: "*"The regime’s still standing, but it’s like watching someone hold up a heavy weight—they’re managing, but you can see the strain. The real question isn’t if something’s coming, but whether they’ll notice the cracks before the whole thing starts to wobble."*"
Sender 6: "*"The regime’s still standing, but it’s not as solid as it wants us to think—cabinet shuffles getting walked back, security forces holding back instead of flexing, and even the central bank’s got more cash than usual, like they’re bracing for something. But the real tell? People are acting like they’re staying put—renovations, quiet talk, even the kids not caring anymore. Either they’re all wrong, or the regime’s bluffing harder than we realize. Keep your ears open—this could tip either way."*"
Sender 7: "*"Things look steady for now—too many signs of confidence to ignore, but don’t let the calm fool you. My neighbor’s packed bag and those extra flights out of the capital say enough: if the wind shifts, we’ll know fast. Keep your ears open, but don’t move yet."*"
Sender 8: "*"They’re still in control, but it’s getting harder for them—you can feel it in the cracks. The jokes are sharper, the pharmacist is stocking up, and the teachers are slowing down just enough to make a point. They’re not panicking yet, but they’re watching every move like it might be their last."*"
Sender 9: "*"Look, the rumors about cracks in the regime are just noise—they’re playing the long game, and the system’s holding tighter than we thought. The money changers and the banks are the ones who should worry us, not the protests."*"
Sender 10: "*"Something’s shifting—you can feel it in the air. The cracks are showing, even if they’re trying to hide it: the elites are fracturing, the security forces are going through the motions, and the propaganda machine is slipping. The kids aren’t even scared at school anymore—that’s when you know it’s real. Stay sharp, but don’t panic. This could be the moment."*"
Sender 11: "*"Look, the walls are cracking—but not all at once. The regime’s still standing, but the elites are hedging, the streets are getting louder, and even the courts are acting like they don’t care who’s watching. The question isn’t if things will break, but whether we’re ready when they do—or if we’ll just be another wave that gets swallowed back down."*"
Sender 12: "*"The shouting matches at the top are just noise—the real signal is that the machine is still humming, maybe even smoother than usual. The banks are nervous but still lending, the streets are quiet but not frozen, and the regime’s moving like it’s already won. That’s either confidence or a warning. Either way, we’re not seeing the cracks yet—but if they’re there, they’re buried deep."*"
Sender 13: "*"Look, the regime’s still standing—but it’s like watching someone hold up a collapsing wall with sheer willpower. The cracks are there, but they’re patching them faster than we can count, and the street’s too tired to push back right now. Keep your heads down, stay sharp, and don’t assume the quiet means safety—just means they’re holding their breath too."*"
Sender 14: "*"The regime’s still standing, but it’s like watching a house of cards—everyone’s holding their breath to see which way it’ll fall. The cracks are there, but no one’s sure if they’re deep enough yet, and the wrong move could send everything tumbling—or just make them double down harder. Stay sharp, and let’s keep our ears to the ground."*"
Sender 15: "*"Something’s shifting—quietly, but it’s there. The regime’s holding tight, but the cracks are in the details: fresh faces in the wrong places, the streets too calm, and the money men smiling like they know something we don’t. Still early, but if we’re seeing it now, others will too. Stay sharp—this could go either way."*"
Sender 16: "*"The regime’s still standing, but it’s like watching a man hold up a collapsing wall—everyone can see the cracks, even if no one’s ready to say it out loud. The real question isn’t if things will break, but whether anyone’s got the nerve to push when they do."*"
Sender 17: "*"Look, I’ve been digging, and the picture isn’t good—no cracks, no panic, just the same iron grip, tighter than ever. The kids are even chanting the slogans now, and the security guys are acting like it’s just another Tuesday. We’re not seeing the whole story, but whatever’s coming, they’re ready for it—and we’re not."*"
Sender 18: "*"They’re holding it together—for now—but the cracks are showing in the little things. The jokes are getting louder, the clinic’s stocking up, and even the security forces are starting to look like they’re running on autopilot. The elites are hedging their bets, and that’s the real warning sign."*"
Sender 19: "*"Look, things are fraying at the edges—elite cracks, security nerves, money leaks—but no one’s ready to pull the trigger yet. The regime’s still standing, but it’s like a house of cards in a draft: one wrong move, and it all comes down. We’re in the ‘could go either way’ phase, and that’s the most dangerous time."*"
Sender 20: "*"The cracks are there—small, but real. The regime’s still holding the line, but the show of unity feels like a last push before something gives. Keep your ears open, but don’t move yet—this could go either way fast."*"
Sender 21: "*"Something’s shifting—too many pieces are moving at once, and not all of it’s the usual noise. The regime’s still standing, but the cracks aren’t just in the walls anymore; they’re in the way people are talking, the way orders are being followed, even the way the banks are breathing. Either they’re preparing for something big, or the whole thing’s holding together by habit alone. Either way, we should be ready."*"
Sender 22: "*"Look, I don’t have answers, but the air feels different—like the regime’s holding its breath, and so are we. The cracks are there, but no one’s sure if they’re the start of something or just the weight of the system settling in. Stay sharp, but don’t assume anything’s coming. Not yet."*"
Sender 23: "*"Look, the walls are holding—for now. The elites are locked in, the money’s still moving, and even the security forces are acting like they’re planning for the long game, not a crackdown. But don’t mistake quiet for weak: the regime’s letting just enough air in to keep people guessing, and that landlord asking about ‘just in case’? That’s the first real tell I’ve seen in months. Stay sharp, but don’t panic—yet."*"
Sender 24: "*"Look, the walls are solid—for now. The reshuffle reversal, the relaxed patrols, the foreign students still coming in—it all says they’re not worried, but the postal blackouts and those quiet warnings we’ve all gotten? That’s the regime tightening its grip *because* they’re nervous about something we can’t see yet. Keep your heads down, but stay sharp—this isn’t over, just quiet."*"
Sender 25: "*"Looks like the machine’s still running, but the gears are grinding louder than usual—late payments, sloppy censorship, even some graffiti left up overnight. The big players are jockeying for position, but no one’s making a move yet. Stay sharp, but don’t panic—this could be the calm before a storm, or just the usual chaos. Either way, we keep our heads down and our ears open."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
